objective: Implement a deterministic, versioned, checkpointable person/episode relationship and lifecycle ledger in CareOps core, retain transfer API compatibility, and exercise the same registry through an ED-facing adapter.
steps: Move PersonId and EpisodeId definitions into identity.rs and re-export from transfer unchanged; preserve constructors and serialized representation.
Implement domain-separated SHA-256 ID derivation from run namespace plus stable typed creation event ID; detect zero/collisions, and do not consume model RNG.

Use exact derivation bytes: core IDs hash ASCII `careops.identity.id.v1\0` + ASCII type tag (`person` or `episode`) + NUL + run namespace u64 big-endian + event key u64 big-endian; first 8 digest bytes interpreted u64 big-endian, zero rejected. ED source-key hash uses ASCII `careops.ed.key.v1\0` + ASCII type tag (`person` or `admission`) + NUL + run namespace u64 BE + UTF-8 byte length u32 BE + exact UTF-8 bytes; no Unicode normalization. Add fixed SHA-256/u64 test vectors and detect all resulting key/ID collisions.

Implement transactional apply_tick batches, canonical ordering, event dedupe/conflict, sealed-time late rejection, typed relationships (BirthParentOf is acyclic; AssociatedWith may cycle), birth provenance and independent episode entry/exit.
Make explicit death reject atomically while any episode is open. Same-tick exits sort before death, but death never fabricates or silently counts exits; record separate lifecycle facts.
Implement checkpoint/restore for IDs, links, episodes, lifecycle records, dedupe payloads and watermark; validate checkpoint graph/cardinality invariants.

Implement an ED adapter over synthetic opaque source keys. Derive spawn/admission keys by domain-separated SHA-256 over run namespace and length-prefixed key bytes; repeated person key reuses PersonId, each distinct admission key creates a new EpisodeId, and hash collisions reject without mutation.

Expose the EpisodeId as the per-episode PathwayPatient subject key; demonstrate distinct maternal/infant pathway completion/censoring, independent transfer records and no cascade after relationship removal in an ED consumer test.
Run the exact core and ED integration test targets, formatting, and reviewer-agent review on the exact integrated commit.

verification.oracle: Core identity contract tests execute and pass, including deterministic IDs, cardinality, atomic failure and checkpoint round-trip.
ED consumer identity adapter preserves compatibility and demonstrates independent maternal/infant progression and transfer identities.

acceptance: A5.1 typed identity/cardinality contract is implemented with stable deterministic IDs, canonical ordering, typed relationship semantics, atomic conflict/cycle rejection and no cascade deletion.

Derivation uses the byte encoding and fixed outputs recorded in this packet; the ED key is opaque byte-exact UTF-8 (no Unicode normalization), empty/oversize keys reject, and zero/colliding IDs fail closed.
BirthParentOf rejects self/transitive cycles; AssociatedWith cycles are permitted and retained.
Service entry creates a new globally unique episode for the stable person; explicit exit closes only that episode; explicit death requires no open episodes and does not synthesize exits.
Maternal and infant persons/episodes use independent pathway subject IDs, progression/outcome results and transfer operations; deleting their relationship has no effect on either record.
ED repeated source person key maps to the same PersonId across distinct admission keys; each new admission maps to a distinct EpisodeId; invalid/empty keys and hash collisions fail closed.
Exact event replay is idempotent; conflicting payload and late post-seal identity events reject atomically without consuming event IDs or RNG.
Checkpoint/restore preserves identity, relationship, lifecycle, dedupe and watermark state; suffix replay matches uninterrupted execution.
The existing careops_core::transfer::{PersonId, EpisodeId} public paths and serialized ID representation remain compatible; no ED scenario/output schema changes.
Reviewer-agent/subagent examines the exact commit against ADR-0014, transfer ownership, pathway streams and both adapters; findings are fixed and re-reviewed.
No Kairos source, parent pin, empirical/clinical validity, portable upstream checkpoint or external delivery guarantee is claimed.
stop_conditions: Existing transfer behavior or serialized compatibility changes
Death/episode accounting or relation-cycle policy cannot satisfy the fixed oracle
Source-key hash collision is not detected atomically
Out-of-scope Kairos or parent pin edit
Required behavior cannot be represented atomically
size_exception: Eleven coordinated paths span a shared identity API, a transfer compatibility re-export, lockfile, core tests and an ED adapter/test. The interface is reviewed before implementation and the paths are committed together; no unrelated source changes are authorized.

ED admission source key to EpisodeEventId
